newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti says H1 figures all in order.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti says H1 figures all in order.

text.p: Italy's troubled information technology group Olivetti on Friday said that its first half 1996 figures published earlier this week were "rigorously" in order.
Earlier this week, a former Olivetti executive said that the figures were misleading.
A Olivetti statement confirmed that net debt at the end of the half year at end-June 1996 was 1.261 trillion lire after 775 billion lire at the end of 1995.

Olivetti published the statement following criticism of its first half 1996 result by Renzo Francesconi the company's former director-general in charge of finance, administration and auditing, and who resigned from Olivetti on Wednesday after only six weeks at the group.
Italy's stock market watchdog Consob met Francesconi on Thursday in Rome to discuse his misgivings over the way Olivetti presented its first half 1996 results this week.

Later on Thursday, Consob met Olivetti officials led by its chief executive Francesco Caio, and after a three and a half hour meeting Caio said Olivetti had presented to Consob all the details to show that Francesconi's comments were groundless. ($ = 1509 Italian Lire)
